title: BoE warns banks to prepare for AI-enabled cyber breaches
key_facts: Sarah Breeden, Deputy Governor of the Bank of England, said on Thursday 15 Oct 2026 the central bank is working with banks on deep cyber-recovery options
She said lenders can no longer assume their defences are impenetrable against AI-enabled cyber attacks
She said AI advances have reached a level at which the technology poses a systemic risk to global financial infrastructure
'Bare metal' systems are fully independent from a bank's main technology set-up and take over if primary systems are compromised
Spoke at the Institute of International Finance annual meeting in Bangkok
UK supervisors have been encouraging the largest banks to examine bare metal recovery plans, Reuters reported on Tuesday
quote_evidence: Bank of England Deputy Governor Sarah Breeden said on Thursday the central bank was working with banks on deep cyber-recovery options, arguing that lenders can no longer assume their defences are impenetrable in the face of AI-enabled cyber attacks.
It's not enough now to assume that the cyber attackers won't get through
why_it_matters_hint: A senior central banker says banks need backup systems that survive a successful AI-powered attack.
